@graph.name: Bag Palletizer
@graph.description: A bag palletizer is a robotic system that picks filled bags from a conveyor and stacks them onto pallets in a set pattern, using end-of-arm tooling selected for the bag type, weight and rate. TRF Industrial Automation builds bag palletizing systems on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Bag Palletizer Handle Different Bag Sizes and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRF palletizing platforms run multiple recipes and pallet patterns, so one bag palletizer can handle more than one bag size or pattern. Each recipe holds the bag data and the pattern for one product, the operator selects it at changeover, and every bag size is validated with its end-of-arm tool and pattern during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Bags?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the bag plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multi-bag picks, the combined weight of the bags. Published case weights are up to about 22 lb for TRFCobot, 44 lb for TRFCompact and 66 lb for TRFSpeed. For bags, TRF validates the payload with your filled bag, tool and pattern, and evaluates a custom palletizer above that range.

mainEntity.name: Can a Bag Palletizer Fit a Plant With Limited Floor Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. TRFCobot has a small footprint for areas where a traditional robotic cell is hard to install, and TRFCompact brings an industrial robot into a compact, standardized cell for brownfield plants. The area for the robot, the infeed pick point, the pallet positions and operator access to remove full pallets is confirmed with your layout, together with the robot reach.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Robotic Bag Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, line speed, bag weight, end-of-arm tool, pallet handling and conveyor integration. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each cost factor.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today, and returns an initial estimate that a TRF Sales Engineer completes with the costs of your project.

mainEntity.name: Who Makes Robotic Bag Palletizers in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF Industrial Automation designs, builds and installs robotic bag palletizers for manufacturers in the United States, on TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or as a custom palletizer. TRF also supplies the conveyors and end-of-line integration around the palletizer, and supports TRF equipment after startup through Parts and Service.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare to Size a Bag Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your line rate in bags per minute, the heaviest and lightest bag weights, the bag construction, your pallet size and target height, the number of bagging lines and a drawing of the floor space. A TRF Sales Engineer uses this data to screen TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or a custom palletizer and to validate the fit before quoting.
